description: Fix cyan screen crashes caused by LVGL thread-safety violations. Diagnostic firmware confirmed the root cause: ui_notify_mqtt_status() and ui_notify_wifi_status() are called directly from background event handlers (MQTT event handler on CPU0, WiFi event handler) without holding the LVGL mutex, racing with the LVGL render task on CPU1. This triggers LV_ASSERT_MSG(!disp->rendering_in_progress) inside lv_inv_area(), which aborts the firmware and leaves the display showing raw uninitialised framebuffer content — visible as cyan on the ST7703 panel. The fix is to route all UI notifications from background tasks through lv_async_call() so they execute safely inside the LVGL task, and to harden the boot sequence so mqtt_task only starts after WiFi has an IP.

userStories.title: Route mqtt_task UI notifications through lv_async_call
userStories.description: As a firmware developer, I want mqtt_task.c to never call LVGL APIs directly from the MQTT event handler so that connect/disconnect events cannot race with the LVGL render task and trigger the rendering_in_progress assert.
acceptanceCriteria: In mqtt_task.c, ui_notify_mqtt_status(true) and ui_notify_mqtt_status(false) are NOT called directly inside mqtt_event_handler()
Both calls are replaced with lv_async_call() trampolines that invoke ui_notify_mqtt_status() from the LVGL task context
The trampoline allocates a small heap struct to pass the bool, frees it after the call
mqtt_task_start() is only called from on_wifi_ip() in main.c (i.e. after WiFi has an IP), not unconditionally at boot — confirm main.c already does this or fix it
userStories.notes: Root cause confirmed by crash decode: Core0 PC 0x4004d8da = lv_inv_area in lv_refr.c:286, assert !disp->rendering_in_progress. mqtt_event_handler fires on the MQTT internal task (CPU0) with no LVGL lock held.

userStories.title: Route wifi_manager UI notifications through lv_async_call
userStories.description: As a firmware developer, I want wifi_manager.c to never call LVGL APIs directly from the WiFi/IP event handler so that wifi status changes cannot race with the LVGL render task.
acceptanceCriteria: In wifi_manager.c, the two direct calls to ui_notify_wifi_status() inside wifi_event_handler() (at WIFI_EVENT_STA_DISCONNECTED and IP_EVENT_STA_GOT_IP) are replaced with lv_async_call() trampolines
The direct call to ui_notify_wifi_status(false, -99, NULL) in wifi_manager_deinit() or any other non-LVGL-task context is also wrapped
Trampoline structs carry all required arguments (connected bool, rssi int, ip string copy)
Existing lv_async_call usage for conn_dispatch and scan_dispatch is left unchanged
userStories.notes: wifi_manager.c already uses lv_async_call for conn_dispatch and scan_dispatch — follow the same pattern for the ui_notify calls.

userStories.title: Validate fix: stress-test navigation without cyan crash
userStories.description: As a firmware developer, I want to confirm the thread-safety fix eliminates the cyan crash by flashing the patched firmware and exercising the UI paths that previously triggered it.
acceptanceCriteria: Flash the patched firmware with idf.py flash
Navigate to Machines tab repeatedly (at least 5 times) — no cyan screen
Navigate between all tabs (Home, Machines, Tanks, People, Debug) in sequence — no cyan screen
Wait for WiFi connect/disconnect cycle (the board retries every ~5s) while on Machines tab — no cyan screen
Take a screenshot with python3 tools/screenshot.py confirming the UI is intact
Serial log shows no LV_ASSERT or abort messages during the test period
userStories.notes: This story is the verification step. If the serial log still shows lv_inv_area crashes, check for any remaining direct LVGL calls from non-LVGL tasks in the codebase (grep for lv_label_set_text, lv_obj_set_style, lv_arc_set_value outside of bsp_display_lock blocks or lv_async_call trampolines).
